title: Automated Generation of Decoders for Irregular Instruction Sets Using Information-Theoretic Decision Tree Construction Algorithms
problem: Manual design of instruction decoders for complex ISAs is tedious and error-prone; existing automated decoder generation tools cannot handle irregular instruction sets with non-uniform opcodes, complex logic propositions, and nested specializations.
motivation: Instruction decoders are critical components of SoC design flows and toolchains; automation reduces manual effort and errors, but ISA irregularities challenge existing tools.
method: Proposes sophisticated decision-tree algorithm based on information-theoretic concepts for automated decoder generation. Algorithm optimizes tree structure considering both functional correctness and performance costs using decision tree generation principles from machine learning.
key_novelty: First information-theoretic decision tree approach for irregular instruction set decoder generation, handling complex logic propositions and nested specializations.
contributions: Decision tree algorithm based on information-theoretic concepts for decoder generation
Handling of irregular ISA features: non-uniform opcodes, logic propositions, nested specializations
Cost-aware decoder optimization for performance and area
Fully automated, functionally correct decoders for SPARC, MIPS32, ARMv7 ISAs
primary_theme: Information-theoretic decoder generation for irregular instruction sets
